name: COMPASS gluon polarisation from high-pT hadron pairs

summary.plain: COMPASS measured how much of the proton's spin could come from the polarisation of its gluons, using photon-gluon fusion events that produce pairs of high-momentum hadrons. The result, consistent with zero within large errors, argued against a large gluon-spin contribution.
summary.technical: Determination of the gluon polarisation Delta G/G in the nucleon from the helicity asymmetry of quasi-real photoproduction events (Q^2 < 1 (GeV/c)^2) with a pair of large transverse-momentum hadrons, using a 160 GeV polarised muon beam on a polarised 6LiD target: A_||/D = 0.002 ± 0.019 (stat) ± 0.003 (syst), giving Delta G/G = 0.024 ± 0.089 (stat) ± 0.057 (syst) at x_g = 0.095 and mu^2 ~ 3 (GeV/c)^2 in a leading-order QCD analysis.

title: Gluon polarization in the nucleon from quasi-real photoproduction of high-pT hadron pairs
why_it_matters: The 'proton spin puzzle' asks how quark spin, gluon spin and orbital motion add up to the proton's spin; a small gluon polarisation at the probed momentum fraction constrains that budget.
